claims.text: Melt spinning at a controlled high cooling rate followed by minimal annealing will refine the lamellar microstructure relative to conventional casting.
This rapid-solidification treatment will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to the conventional as-cast state.
Conventionally cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has an fcc/B2 dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The lamellar microstructure of conventionally cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is coarse.
Minimal post-process annealing can relieve residual stresses without significant microstructural coarsening.
The proposed improvement should hold at room temperature under structural load-bearing conditions.
Rapid solidification will decrease the interlamellar spacing.
Rapid solidification will enhance phase-interface coherence between the soft and hard phases.
The eutectic alloy concept produces alternating soft fcc and hard bcc/B2 phases.
Refined lamellae promote more cooperative deformation between the constituent phases.
Refined lamellae reduce stress concentrations and improve load sharing.
Reduced stress concentrations and improved load sharing increase ductility.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can exhibit a combination of high tensile ductility and high fracture strength at room temperature.
Strength and ductility commonly present a trade-off in structural materials and HEAs.
Eutectic HEAs made by traditional casting and conventional heat treatment typically display the strength-ductility trade-off.
Insufficient cooling-rate control or inadequate residual-stress relief can eliminate the proposed benefit.
The treatment's effectiveness will vary with alloy composition and processing parameters.

contradictions.description: The comparator is not consistent: the hypothesis specifies a conventional as-cast baseline, whereas the baseline and experimental design include conventional heat treatment.
